summary: Completed the mock-first correction of the Android MVP backlog: US-007 and US-008 were rewritten to run exclusively on the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository (no GET/POST /api/incidents, HTTP, JWT, Keystore or INTERNET permission), the stale activity diagrams of US-006, US-009 and US-011 were replaced with their local mock flows, and US-005's previously empty security and NFR sections now explicitly define zero permissions, no external calls, no embedded credentials, demo-credentials-only, deterministic mocks, fast offline builds, reproducible tests and an installable debug APK. The parent hierarchy was aligned (FEAT-005/006/007 and FEAT-009 renamed and re-described as mock-only with real integration deferred to US-012; EPIC-002 described as the mock-first MVP; EPIC-003 reduced to debug-APK delivery with all release-signing requirements removed), US-012 remains the single non-blocking follow-up owning all real transport, and every touched story re-passed the eight-point quality audit with honest quality fields.

operations.description: The native Android product surface for AndersonMobile employees, delivered mock-first: a Kotlin + Jetpack Compose app (com.nexti.minisoporte, minSdk 26, Spanish, portrait) that runs the complete employee journey — sign in, report incidents, review only their own reports, sign out — entirely on in-memory fake repositories with deterministic seeded data, fake admin/admin authentication and an in-memory TokenStore. The mock MVP declares ZERO permissions, makes no network calls and requires no backend; this is the only user-facing component of MiniSoporte v1 and it renders the approved Pre-Design screens without any server dependency. Real-backend integration — Retrofit/OkHttp, DTOs, mappers, AuthInterceptor, the INTERNET permission, JWT sessions, Keystore-backed token storage and every real FastAPI endpoint — is the single deferred non-blocking follow-up story US-012, on which no mock story depends.

The operational backbone that makes the product reproducible and deliverable for internal testing: the idempotent demo seed provisioning demo accounts and incidents outside production, the pytest quality gate proving authentication, ownership isolation and role protection at >=90% business-logic coverage, and the mock-first Android delivery contract — an installable, unsigned debug APK (app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk) built from apps/mobile with ./gradlew check :app:assembleDebug and copied manually to reviewer devices. The current MVP requires no release signing: no keystore files, no key.properties, no ANDROID_KEY* environment variables and no Google Play publication — release signing and store submission remain deliberate external actions outside the mock MVP.

The S-01 entry screen and the client-side session machinery, implemented mock-first: required-field validation with Spanish per-field errors, the demo hint box showing admin/admin, generic failure messaging with a submit lock, and sign-out (delivered with S-02). Authentication runs exclusively against the in-memory FakeAuthService from US-005 accepting exactly admin/admin, and the fake session token lives only in the in-memory TokenStore fake — no POST /api/auth/login, no HTTP 401/422/429 handling, no JWT, no Android Keystore and no network. Real authentication (login endpoint, rate limits, expired-token recovery, Keystore-backed persistence) is deferred to US-012. - Spanish form with required-field errors (BR-001) validated client-side only in the mock MVP. - Generic error that never hints whether an account exists, even against the fake (INSTR-007, BR-002). - No 401 handling exists in the mock MVP — the expired-token recovery path arrives with US-012.

The S-02 home screen after sign-in, implemented mock-first on the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository seeded by US-005: the signed-in mock user's own incidents newest-first as compact cards, status filter chips with live counts, loading/empty/error+retry states, the accent FAB to create, and the Salir sign-out that clears only the in-memory mock session and returns to S-01. No GET /api/incidents, no HTTP responses, no JWT and no Android Keystore — the real REST list contract is delivered by US-012. - Owner-scoped rendering enforced by the fake repository under every filter (FUNC-003, INSTR-001). - Filter chips Todas/Pendiente/En progreso/Resuelta with live count badges computed over the seeded list (FUNC-004). - Sign-out clears the in-memory mock session token; protected screens unreachable afterwards (FUNC-002, BR-005).

The two drill-down screens of the review experience, implemented mock-first against the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository: S-03 Nueva incidencia with live per-field validation, character counters and a duplicate-submission lock creating incidents in memory (always Pendiente, with the initial history entry), and S-04 Detalle de incidencia with the full incident card plus the newest-first status-history timeline and a safe no-access state for foreign identifiers. No POST /api/incidents, no GET /api/incidents/{id}, no HTTP responses, no JWT and no Android Keystore — the real API integration is deferred to US-012. - Creation always yields a Pendiente mock incident with local field-level validation and deterministic results (FUNC-005, INSTR-002). - Detail shows identifier, full data and the read-only newest-first history timeline from the seeded fake (FUNC-006, BR-021). - Missing/foreign ids render the safe no-access state — the UI never leaks another mock user's incident (BR-010).

operations.title: Installable Internal-Test Debug APK (No Release Signing)
operations.description: Completes the mock-first distribution story for internal testing: the build contract that produces the installable app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk from apps/mobile via ./gradlew check :app:assembleDebug with zero signing secrets, a monotonic versionCode with a human-readable versionName, and a build-only run entry. There is no release signing configuration in the mock MVP — no keystore files, no key.properties, no ANDROID_KEY* variables and no signed release APK — and no publication of any kind. - Installable app-debug.apk for manual internal distribution from a clean machine with zero secrets (CONF-010, BR-037). - check/assembleDebug remain the only required build tasks; no production secrets are ever needed. - No publication: internal testing only; store submission and release signing stay deliberate external actions (BR-038).

security_considerations: The Android manifest declares ZERO permissions: no android.permission.INTERNET, no dangerous permissions and no deep links — the mock app makes no external calls of any kind and no data leaves the device (BR-031, CONF-007); the INTERNET permission is added only by US-012.

No external calls: no network stack exists in this story's code path — no Retrofit, OkHttp, HTTP client, DTO or backend endpoint is reachable from debug builds, previews or tests; all data access resolves in memory through the fake seams.

No embedded production credentials: no secrets, passwords, API keys, keystores or key.properties exist in the source, the version catalog or the built APK — there is nothing to leak and nothing committed (BR-039 convention).

Demo credentials only for the mock build: FakeAuthService accepts exactly username admin / password admin, exists only in the mock/debug MVP, is displayed on S-01 by design, and never grants access to real data — the real authentication path is US-012.
The fake session token is held only in the in-memory TokenStore fake, never logged and never rendered in UiState (CONF-002, mock-phase BR-006); no Android Keystore code exists in this story.
non_functional_requirements: Deterministic in-memory mocks: FakeAuthService and FakeIncidentRepository are seeded with fixed data, produce identical results on every run and resolve effectively instantly, making UI flows and tests reproducible (Q-005, BR-041).
Fast local build: ./gradlew check :app:assembleDebug completes without any backend, database, network connection or secrets and produces app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk.

Reproducible tests: the check suite (unit + Compose component tests, ktlint, Android Lint) runs fully offline and is pinned by the version catalog and Gradle wrapper, so results are identical on any machine (BR-037).
Installable debug APK: every check run yields an app-debug.apk installable on a portrait phone, demoable end-to-end on the mock journey with zero environment setup (CONF-010, BR-040).
operations.gate_note: All eight checks pass after filling the previously empty security and NFR sections: the narrative keeps actor/trigger/outcome; the functional flow covers the happy path plus the simulated failure/retry behavior; design traceability explains the absent screens/apis/entities/flows; the technical analysis carries the full contract for every traced artifact; the rules are story-specific and the new security considerations (zero permissions, no external calls, no embedded credentials, mock-only demo credentials) and NFRs (deterministic mocks, fast offline build, reproducible tests, installable debug APK) are explicit and testable; the acceptance criteria are sufficient and testable; related claim ids exist in traceability; and the empty dependency list is valid for the first mobile story.

All eight checks pass after replacing the stale diagram: the activity diagram now shows the local mock sign-in flow only (FakeAuthService + in-memory TokenStore, admin/admin, generic failure) with no POST /api/auth/login, no 401/422/429 branches and no Keystore step, agreeing with the narrative, functional flow, rich fields and business rules; the remaining checks (actor/trigger/outcome, wrong-credential alternate path, design traceability with explained absent APIs, technical contract, story-specific rules/security/NFRs, testable criteria, real claim ids, and the single US-005 dependency in valid order) were re-verified and hold.

operations.title: S-02 Mis incidencias: owned list with status filter chips, states and sign-out
operations.description: Implements the S-02 home screen exclusively on the mock foundation: the signed-in mock user's own seeded incidents newest-first as compact cards (title, category pill, priority pill, status badge, creation date), status filter chips with live counts, loading/empty/error+retry states, the accent FAB to S-03, and the Salir sign-out that clears only the in-memory mock session. All data comes from the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository — no GET /api/incidents, no HTTP responses, no JWT, no Android Keystore and no INTERNET permission; the real REST list contract is delivered by US-012.
operations.narrative: As an AndersonMobile employee testing the mock MVP, I see only my own seeded incidents on S-02 — newest first as compact cards with title, category, priority, status badge and creation date — and I can filter them with status chips showing live counts, so that I can quickly find the report I care about; from here I can also open the create form via the FAB and sign out via Salir, which clears the in-memory mock session so no protected screen stays reachable. Trigger: navigation to S-02 after mock sign-in, screen re-entry, chip tap, card tap, or Salir tap. Every read resolves against the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository from US-005 — no network request is ever made; the real GET /api/incidents contract and all transport behavior are deferred to US-012.
operations.functional_flow: 1. On S-02 entry the ViewModel loads the incident list through the repository seam exclusively from the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository (no GET /api/incidents, no HTTP) — owner-scoped to the signed-in mock user, newest first, no pagination. 2. The list renders as cards (title + status badge, category pill, priority pill, 'Creada el <date>'); loading, empty ('Sin incidencias') and error+retry states cover every load outcome; the retry path is exercised via the fake's simulated failure capability (CONF-009 convention established by US-005), not by network errors. 3. Tapping a filter chip (Todas/Pendiente/En progreso/Resuelta) re-queries the fake with the status filter and updates every chip's live count badge; filtering never exposes another mock user's incidents. 4. Tapping a card navigates to S-04. 5. Tapping the FAB opens S-03. 6. Tapping 'Salir' clears the in-memory mock session (deletes the fake token from the in-memory TokenStore fake — no server endpoint, no Keystore, mock-phase BR-005), shows the confirmation toast 'Sesión cerrada' and routes to S-01; no protected screen remains accessible afterward (BR-005). Out of scope (US-012): the real GET /api/incidents contract, HTTP responses, expired-token recovery and any network behavior — no such logic exists in the mock MVP.
acceptance_criteria: CA-01: Given the signed-in mock user owns 3 seeded incidents (mixed statuses), When S-02 loads from the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository, Then exactly those 3 cards render newest-first, each with title, category pill, priority pill, status badge and 'Creada el <date>' (BR-019, BR-009).

CA-02: Given the load is in flight, When S-02 is entered, Then the loading state renders; given the owned list for the active filter is empty, Then the 'Sin incidencias' empty state renders (FUNC-003).

CA-03: Given the fake's simulated failure mode (CONF-009 convention from US-005), When the load fails, Then the error state renders with a retry button and tapping retry reloads from the fake without crashing — no network error path exists in this story.

CA-04: Given the chips Todas/Pendiente/En progreso/Resuelta, When a chip is tapped, Then the list narrows to that status, the active chip is filled dark green, and every chip's live count badge updates from the seeded list (FUNC-004, BR-017).

CA-05: Given seeded incidents for more than one mock user, When the signed-in mock user filters or reloads, Then no card, count, or detail path ever exposes another mock user's data (BR-009, INSTR-001).

CA-06: Given 'Salir' is tapped, When sign-out completes, Then the fake session token is deleted from the in-memory TokenStore fake (nothing readable remains), the toast 'Sesión cerrada' shows, and the app routes to S-01 with no protected screen reachable — no Keystore, no JWT and no network call involved (FUNC-002, mock-phase BR-005).
CA-07: Given a status badge, When rendered, Then it always shows its Spanish label together with its paired background color — never color alone (INSTR-012, BR-036).

CA-08: Given the test suites, When ./gradlew check runs, Then the list/filter ViewModel state-machine tests over the fake and s02_* Compose component tests pass fully offline, and journeys 2 and 5 of the five mandatory mock journeys hold.

CA-09: Given the story scope, When inspected, Then no real API contract logic exists — no GET /api/incidents, no HTTP responses, no JWT, no Android Keystore, no INTERNET permission — these are explicitly deferred to US-012, and this story depends only on US-005 and US-006.
business_rules: BR-005 (mock-phase) — Signing out clears the in-memory mock session (the fake token is deleted from the in-memory TokenStore fake), and no protected screen remains accessible afterward; no server endpoint, JWT or Keystore exists in the mock MVP (FUNC-002, Q-008).
BR-009 — The list shows only incidents the signed-in mock user owns; the fake enforces owner isolation under every filter (INSTR-001).
BR-017 — Statuses limited to the fixed set pending/in_progress/resolved; filter options are All, Pending, In progress, Resolved.
BR-019 — Own incidents, newest first, each card showing title, category, priority, status, and creation date.
BR-020 — No pagination in v1: all owned seeded incidents matching the filter are rendered.
BR-036 — Statuses differentiated with text and color — never color alone; palette/contrast/touch-target baseline (INSTR-012).
BR-041 — Mock-first: the only data source for S-02 is the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository; no network, backend or HTTP transport is required or present.
security_considerations: Sign-out is a local in-memory operation only: it deletes the fake session token from the in-memory TokenStore fake and involves no server, no JWT and no Keystore (mock-phase BR-005).
The UI can only render owner-scoped fake data; the fake scopes every read to the signed-in mock user and filtering cannot widen scope (INSTR-001, BR-009).
No network calls and no INTERNET permission in this story — mock data never leaves the device and nothing can be intercepted in transit.
Token material (the fake session token) is never logged and never rendered in UiState (CONF-002, mock-phase BR-006).
non_functional_requirements: Deterministic in-memory reads resolve effectively instantly (<2 s budget trivially met) and produce identical results on every run; list rendering in LazyColumn with stable keys for smooth scrolling.
Loading/empty/error states on the screen at all times; retry always available via the fake's simulated failure convention (CONF-009).
48dp touch targets; pill chips 999px radius; light theme tokens only (BR-036); no backend or network connectivity required.

Compose component tests with s02_* tags: cards render title/category/priority/status/date, chips filter and show live counts, status badge text + color.

technical_analysis.flow_slice: Incident review flow (mock-first) — Step 1: On S-02 entry the ViewModel loads the list through the repository seam exclusively from the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository; the fake returns only incidents owned by the signed-in mock user (INSTR-001, BR-009), newest-first with no pagination (BR-020); list items omit description. S-02 renders each card with title, category, priority, status badge, and 'Creada el <date>', plus loading / empty ('Sin incidencias') / error+retry states. Step 2: The employee taps a filter chip (Todas / Pendiente / En progreso / Resuelta); the ViewModel re-queries the fake with the status filter (FUNC-004) and count badges update live. Outcome & errors: an empty result set shows the 'Sin incidencias' state (normal edge case); the error+retry state is exercised via the fake's simulated failure (CONF-009) — no network failure path exists in the mock MVP. Session lifecycle — Step 3: The employee taps 'Salir' on S-02; sign-out clears the fake session token from the in-memory TokenStore fake only (FUNC-002, mock-phase BR-005), shows the confirmation toast 'Sesión cerrada', and returns to S-01 with no protected screen reachable afterward. No JWT, no Keystore and no HTTP request are involved anywhere; the real transport behavior is deferred to US-012.
technical_analysis.notes: The FAB's navigation to S-03 is wired here; the create screen itself is US-008, and the card -> S-04 drill-down is completed by US-009. Chip counts derive from the currently loaded owned list (client-side counts over the fake's array, refreshed on load).

operations.gate_note: All eight checks pass after the mock-first rewrite: the narrative has actor (employee/tester), trigger (navigation/chip/card/FAB/Salir) and outcome (owned newest-first list or sign-out to S-01); the functional flow covers the happy path plus the empty and simulated-failure alternates while explicitly scoping the real endpoint and 401 handling to US-012; design traceability covers components, the S-02 screen and both flows and explains why apis/entities are empty; the technical analysis carries the full screen spec, conventions and test strategy for the traced artifacts with zero endpoint contracts; rules, security and NFRs are story-specific to the fake-backed mock path with no HTTP/JWT/Keystore residue; the acceptance criteria are sufficient and testable including the no-real-API scope guard (CA-09); related claim ids exist in traceability; and dependencies (US-005, US-006) are real stories in valid build order.

operations.title: S-03 Nueva incidencia: validated creation form with counters and duplicate-submission lock
operations.description: Implements the S-03 creation screen exclusively in memory through the FakeIncidentRepository from US-005: the employee fills Título, Categoría, Prioridad and Descripción with live per-field validation and character counters, and a valid submit creates a deterministic mock incident that always starts in Pendiente with its initial history entry, returning to S-02 with the new card first. No POST /api/incidents, no HTTP 401/422, no network errors, no JWT and no Android Keystore — the real API implementation is delivered by US-012.
operations.narrative: As an AndersonMobile employee testing the mock MVP, I can report a new incident on S-03 by filling Título, Categoría, Prioridad and Descripción with live validation and character counters, so that my report is accepted complete and correct (always starting in Pendiente) and I return to my list seeing it first; invalid input shows Spanish errors next to each field and never creates a partial mock incident. Trigger: tapping the accent FAB on S-02. Creation happens exclusively in the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository — no POST /api/incidents request is ever made; the real API contract and transport behavior are deferred to US-012.
operations.functional_flow: 1. The employee fills Título (live 'n / 100' counter), Categoría choice group (Sistemas/Equipos/Acceso/Otro), Prioridad choice group (Baja/Media/Alta) and Descripción (live 'n / 1000' counter); a hint states the incident will be created in 'Pendiente' state (INSTR-002). 2. Live per-field validation enforces the rules locally (title 5–100 chars, description 10–1000 chars, category and priority required — BR-013..016); Spanish errors render next to each field (INSTR-011) and submission is blocked. 3. Tapping 'Guardar incidencia' locks the button with the label 'Guardando…' (duplicate-submission lock) and creates the incident exclusively in the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository — no POST /api/incidents, no HTTP; the fake always sets status Pendiente and records the initial history entry (previous_status null), ignoring any status/owner input (INSTR-002, BR-011). 4. On success the app returns to S-02 with a confirmation toast and the new 'Pendiente' incident appears first (newest-first, BR-019). Out of scope (US-012): the real POST /api/incidents contract, HTTP 401/422 handling, server-side authoritative validation and network failure/retry behavior — no network request is ever made in the mock MVP.
acceptance_criteria: CA-01: Given the form, When the employee types in Título or Descripción, Then live 'n / 100' and 'n / 1000' counters update with each keystroke.

CA-02: Given a title of 4 or 101 chars, or a description of 9 or 1001 chars, When local validation runs, Then Spanish field-level errors render next to the offending fields, submit is blocked, and nothing is created in the fake (BR-013, BR-014).
CA-03: Given no category or no priority selected, When the employee taps Guardar incidencia, Then the required-choice errors render and nothing is submitted (BR-015, BR-016).

CA-04: Given a valid form, When Guardar incidencia is tapped, Then the button locks with the label 'Guardando…' and repeated taps produce exactly one creation in the in-memory FakeIncidentRepository (duplicate-submission lock).

CA-05: Given a valid submission, When the in-memory creation resolves, Then the fake stores exactly one mock incident with status Pendiente (created_at == updated_at and an initial history entry with previous_status null), the app navigates back to S-02 with a confirmation toast, and the new 'Pendiente' card appears first in the list (BR-019, INSTR-002).

CA-06: Given deterministic repeated runs of the same valid submission against a freshly seeded fake, When creation executes, Then the mock result is identical every time — the created incident and its initial history entry are fully deterministic.
CA-07: Given the test suites, When ./gradlew check runs, Then the ViewModel validation tests and s03_* Compose tests pass fully offline, and journey 3 of the five mandatory mock journeys holds.

CA-08: Given the story scope, When inspected, Then no real API contract logic exists — no POST /api/incidents, no HTTP 401/422 handling, no network error path, no JWT, no Android Keystore — these are explicitly deferred to US-012, and this story depends only on US-005 and US-007.
business_rules: BR-011 — Every incident created starts in Pending status; the form hints 'Pendiente', never submits a status, and the fake always sets it (INSTR-002).
BR-013 — Title required, 5–100 characters, validated live in the mock MVP.
BR-014 — Description required, 10–1,000 characters, with live counter; validated locally in the mock MVP (server-authoritative validation arrives with US-012).
BR-015 — Category in the fixed set Systems/Equipment/Access/Other (choice group).
BR-016 — Priority in the fixed set Low/Medium/High (choice group).
BR-018 — Local field-level validation with Spanish errors; a failed validation never creates the incident in the fake (INSTR-011); the client+server validation pair is completed by US-012.
BR-041 — Mock-first: creation runs exclusively against the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository; no network or backend is required or present.
Duplicate-submission lock: the submit button is disabled with label 'Guardando…' while the in-memory creation resolves (draft behavior, FUNC-005).
security_considerations: The client never sends status/owner fields; the fake ignores them and always sets Pendiente and the signed-in mock owner — the mass-assignment backstop on the real server arrives with US-012 (INSTR-002).
Input validation is enforced locally for immediate feedback; no user input leaves the device in the mock MVP (INSTR-011, BR-018).
No network calls, no INTERNET permission and no credential material in this story — nothing is transmitted, and no token material is kept in UiState (CONF-002, mock-phase BR-006).
non_functional_requirements: Deterministic in-memory creation: identical input on a freshly seeded fake yields an identical mock incident and history entry, keeping tests and demos reproducible (Q-005, BR-041).
48dp targets, live counters within the 8dp grid, theme tokens only (BR-036); no backend or network connectivity required.
Validation is debounce-free and unit-testable in the ViewModel without Compose; the fake creation resolves effectively instantly so the 'Guardando…' lock is exercisable in tests.

design_traceability.notes: Mobile half of the creation flow rendered against the in-memory fake: APIs are [] because the real POST /api/incidents contract is realized by US-012 — the mock story creates incidents deterministically in memory only. Entities [] — the fake holds the created incident in memory for the session; the client persists nothing locally.

conventions: Feature package ui/newincident: NewIncidentScreen.kt with NewIncidentViewModel.kt; validation logic (title 5–100, description 10–1000, required category/priority) lives in the ViewModel, unit-testable without Compose; the UI only renders the resulting field-error state and char counters.

rememberSaveable only for trivial UI state (form field text), never for session/data state (that lives in the ViewModel); stateless composables with UiState + event lambdas; one-shot events (navigation on success, toast) emitted as consumed events.

Choice-group options and buttons are theme-token styled; no hard-coded hex/DP; 48dp minimum touch targets; per-field error semantics announced via liveRegion; test tags s03_* (e.g. s03_title_input, s03_submit).

Duplicate-submission lock in the ViewModel (submitting flag) with the button label switching to 'Guardando…'; submission goes through the IncidentRepository seam wired to the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository — no Retrofit, OkHttp, DTO, JWT or network code is reachable from this screen.

The client never sends status/owner fields; the fake always sets status Pendiente, a fresh mock id, created_at == updated_at and the initial history entry (previous_status null), mirroring the future server behavior so the US-012 swap cannot change the UI contract (INSTR-002, BR-011).
test_strategy: ViewModel unit tests: title 5–100 and description 10–1000 boundary validation with counters, required category/priority, duplicate-submission lock producing exactly one fake creation.

Fake behavior tests: a valid submit inserts exactly one Pendiente mock incident with created_at == updated_at and an initial history entry (previous_status null); the new incident appears first in the owned list (newest-first); repeated identical submissions on a freshly seeded fake are deterministic.
Compose component tests with s03_* tags: counters, field-level Spanish errors, 'Guardando…' lock, navigation back to S-02 with the new Pendiente card first.
./gradlew check passes with no backend, no network, no secrets.
technical_analysis.flow_slice: Incident creation flow (mock-first) — Trigger: On S-02, the employee taps the accent FAB ('+') opening S-03. Step 1: fill 'Título' (live 'n / 100' counter), 'Categoría' choice group, 'Prioridad' choice group, 'Descripción' (live 'n / 1000' counter); live per-field validation enforces the title 5–100 and description 10–1000 rules and required choices locally (BR-013..016); a hint states the incident will be created in 'Pendiente' state (INSTR-002). Step 2: tap 'Guardar incidencia'; the button locks with the label 'Guardando…' (duplicate-submission lock). Step 3: the ViewModel submits through the repository seam to the deterministic in-memory FakeIncidentRepository — no HTTP request is made; the fake always assigns status Pendiente, a fresh mock id, created_at == updated_at and the initial history entry (previous_status null), and never accepts status/owner input (INSTR-002, BR-011). Step 4: on success the app returns to S-02, shows a confirmation, and the new 'Pendiente' incident appears at the top of the list (BR-019). Outcome & errors: invalid fields block submission with Spanish per-field errors and nothing is created (INSTR-011, BR-018) — validation is entirely local, so no 401/422 path exists in the mock MVP. The real POST /api/incidents contract, server-side validation and transport behavior are deferred to US-012.
technical_analysis.notes: The FakeIncidentRepository simulates the same contract in memory, including the initial history entry (previous_status null), so the flow demos without a backend (Q-005, deterministic results). The client never sends status/owner fields — creation is always Pendiente (INSTR-002, BR-011). The server-authoritative validation and mass-assignment backstop arrive with US-012.
